summary: This note describes the system-defined, read-only SNOWFLAKE database, which holds metadata and historical usage data about objects in an organization and its accounts. It lists the schemas inside the database, including ACCOUNT_USAGE, ORGANIZATION_USAGE, DATA_SHARING_USAGE and READER_ACCOUNT_USAGE, and notes that the database is visible to all users while many of its objects require explicit access grants by an ACCOUNTADMIN.
one_line: Describes Snowflake's read-only SNOWFLAKE database, its schemas of usage and metadata views, and its access rules.
key_facts: Snowflake provides a system-defined, read-only shared database named SNOWFLAKE that contains metadata and historical usage data about the objects in an organization and its accounts.

In each account, the SNOWFLAKE database contains read-only schemas including ACCOUNT_USAGE, ALERT, CORE, DATA_PRIVACY, DATA_SHARING_USAGE, INFORMATION_SCHEMA, ORGANIZATION_USAGE, READER_ACCOUNT_USAGE and ML.
The ACCOUNT_USAGE schema contains views that display object metadata and usage metrics for an account.
The CORE schema contains views and other schema objects used in select Snowflake features and currently only contains the system tags used by data objects.
The DATA_SHARING_USAGE schema contains views that display object metadata and usage metrics related to listings published in the Snowflake Marketplace or a data exchange.
The INFORMATION_SCHEMA schema is automatically created in all databases; in a shared database such as SNOWFLAKE, it doesn't serve a purpose and can be disregarded.
The ORGANIZATION_USAGE schema contains views that display historical usage data across all the accounts in an organization.
The READER_ACCOUNT_USAGE schema is similar to ACCOUNT_USAGE but only contains views relevant to the reader accounts provisioned for the account.
Some SNOWFLAKE schemas include classes, which are extensible object types that encapsulate object data and code.
By default, the SNOWFLAKE database is visible to all users, but this does not mean all objects within it are accessible to all users.

Objects not meant to be accessible by default remain inaccessible unless access is explicitly granted by a user with the ACCOUNTADMIN role, including access to the ACCOUNT_USAGE, READER_ACCOUNT_USAGE, ORGANIZATION_USAGE, and DATA_SHARING_USAGE schemas.
Privileges to perform other actions on these views can be granted to other roles in the account.
